detail.longDescription: I am a BS Artificial Intelligence student at Riphah International University, Pakistan, and I am working on an air quality monitoring and prediction project. The idea is to develop an IoT-based device that monitors air quality in homes. Initially, I am using PM2.5 and PM10 sensors, and I want to use their readings to predict other pollutants, including: SO2 NO2 CO O3 I have explored several air quality datasets, including the Beijing Multi-Site Air Quality Dataset , but I am facing difficulties getting good prediction results. I have tried different ANN architectures, preprocessing techniques, feature engineering, and fine-tuning pretrained models. However, the R² scores for some pollutants are still very low and sometimes even negative. I think one possible reason is that the available datasets do not provide enough relevant input features for predicting these pollutants accurately. I would like to know: Are there any other reliable air quality datasets that contain all these pollutants along with useful environmental features? Apart from PM2.5 and PM10, which additional features would be most useful for predicting SO2, NO2, CO, and O3? Would adding temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind speed, wind direction, and historical readings improve the predictions? Is it practically possible to predict these pollutants using only PM2.5 and PM10, or would additional sensors be necessary? Since my actual hardware device will initially measure only PM2.5 and PM10, I am trying to find a suitable approach that can work with these limitations. I would appreciate any suggestions, especially from people who have worked with air quality datasets or pollutant prediction models.
